'''Federico Ardila''' (born 1977) is a [[Colombians|Colombian]] [[mathematician]] who is also active as a [[DJ]]. His research is in [[combinatorics]], with a focus on [[matroid theory]]. Ardila is currently a professor at [[Queen Mary University of London]], and has also held roles at [[San Francisco State University]] and the [[University of the Andes (Colombia)|University of the Andes]].<ref name=":02">{{Cite web|url=http://math.sfsu.edu/federico/|title=federico ardila|website=math.sfsu.edu|access-date=2020-02-14|archive-date=2020-02-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224002119/http://math.sfsu.edu/federico/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":03">{{Cite web|url=https://www.seresearch.qmul.ac.uk/ccant/news/5263/professor-federico-ardila-joining-qmul-in-january-2026/|title=Professor Federico Ardila joining QMUL in January 2026|website=QMUL Faculty of Science and Engineering - Research}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Ardila was born in [[Bogotá|Bogotá, Colombia]].<ref name=quanta>{{Cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematician-federico-ardila-dances-to-the-joys-and-sorrows-of-discovery-20171120/|title=Mathematician Federico Ardila Dances to the Joys and Sorrows of Discovery|website=Quanta Magazine|date=20 November 2017 |language=en|access-date=14 February 2020}}</ref> While at [[Colegio San Carlos]], Ardila represented [[Colombia]] twice in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], winning bronze in 1993 and silver in 1994.<ref name=imo>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=839 |title=Federico Ardila Mantilla |website=[[International Mathematical Olympiads]] |language=en |access-date=4 May 2020 }}</ref>

Ardila earned a degree in mathematics from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in 1998 and completed his PhD in 2003 under [[Richard P. Stanley]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Federico Ardila - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=71550 |access-date=2026-03-22 |website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

Beyond mathematics, Ardila is a co-founder of the DJ collective, La Pelanga.<ref name=quanta/>

== Career ==
Ardila has written about increasing representation in [[mathematics]] and proposed principles for inclusive learning environments, which he calls 'The Axioms'.<ref name=":02" /><ref name="todoscuentan">{{Cite journal |url=https://www.ams.org/publications/journals/notices/201610/rnoti-p1164.pdf |title=Todos Cuentan: Cultivating Diversity in Combinatorics |last=Ardila |first=Federico |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |date=November 2016 |volume=63 |number=10 |language=en |pages=1164–1170 |doi=10.1090/noti1434  |doi-access=free|pmid=28607525 |pmc=5466815 |access-date=4 May 2020 }}</ref>

He established the SFSU-Colombia Combinatorics Initiative, a collaborative program between [[San Francisco State University]] and the [[University of the Andes (Colombia)|Universidad de los Andes]], and "Todos Cuentan," a community-based project aimed at supporting mathematicians from underrepresented backgrounds.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://math.sfsu.edu/federico/SFSUColombia/que.html |title=federico ardila . sfsu-colombia combinatorics initiative |website=math.sfsu.edu |access-date=2020-02-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151022144026/https://math.sfsu.edu/federico/SFSUColombia/que.html |archive-date=22 October 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He has published over 200 hours of free lectures and mathematical  resources online.<ref name="sfstatemagazine">{{cite magazine |last=Bruntz |first=Michael |date=Fall 2010 |title=A World-Class Education |url=http://math.sfsu.edu/federico/SFSUColombia/Press/SFState.pdf |magazine=SF State Magazine |pages=16–17 |access-date=4 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014230148/http://math.sfsu.edu/federico/SFSUColombia/Press/SFState.pdf |archive-date=14 October 2021 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Michael E. Moody Lecture Series |url=https://www.hmc.edu/mathematics/activities/moody-lecture-series/ |website=Harvey Mudd College |access-date=2026-04-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Federico Ardila – Personal Profile |url=https://www.slmath.org/people/11876 |website=Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute |access-date=2026-04-11}}</ref> He has also made several appearances in the mathematical [[YouTube]] video series ''[[Numberphile]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Geometry, Robots and Society |url=https://physics.berkeley.edu/news-events/events/geometry-robots-and-society |website=UC Berkeley Physics |date=23 February 2022}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* One of the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]] (2020)<ref name=maa>{{cite web |url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/haimo-award-distinguished-teaching |title=Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award |website=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=4 May 2020 |archive-date=7 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507072419/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/haimo-award-distinguished-teaching |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[Simons Foundation]] Fellowship in Mathematics (2019–2020)<ref name=simons>{{cite web |url=https://www.ipam.ucla.edu/news/simons-foundation-announces-2019-fellows/ |title=Simons Foundation Announces 2019 Fellows |website=[[Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics]] |date=17 May 2019 |access-date=4 May 2020 }}</ref>
* Premio Nacional de Matemáticas of the [[Colombian Mathematical Society]] (2019)<ref name=premio>{{cite web |url=http://scm.org.co/ganadores-premios-de-matematicas-2019/ |title=¿Quiénes son los ganadores de los Premios de Matemáticas 2019? |last=Padilla |first=Sara |website=Sociedad Colombiana de Matemáticas |access-date=4 May 2020 |language=Spanish }}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2018)<ref name=ams>{{cite web |url=https://news.sfsu.edu/news-story/professor-named-fellow-american-mathematical-society |title=Professor named a fellow of the American Mathematical Society |last=Monahan |first=Patrick |website=[[San Francisco State University]] |access-date=4 May 2020 |date=21 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190302134232/https://news.sfsu.edu/news-story/professor-named-fellow-american-mathematical-society |archive-date=2 March 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[National Science Foundation CAREER Award]] (2010–2016)<ref name=nsf>{{cite web |url=https://nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0956178 |title=CAREER: Matroids, polytopes, and their valuations in algebra and geometry |website=[[National Science Foundation]] |access-date=4 May 2020 }}</ref>
